title: Profit is not cash: the 13-week cash flow check
purpose: Educational short; supports the live product '13-Week Cash Flow Forecast for Small Business' (B14-001). Internal review pilot, not authorized for publication.

scenes.heading: Profit is not cash

visual.label: can be the bank balance, even in a profitable month

lines: A business can be profitable and still run out of cash.
Profit counts a sale when you invoice. Cash counts it when the money arrives.

scenes.heading: Where the gap comes from

items: Rent, payroll and suppliers are due now
Big one-off bills arrive in the same week

lines: Customers often pay thirty to sixty days after the invoice.
Rent, payroll and suppliers are due on fixed dates.
And a large one-off bill can land in the same week.

scenes.heading: The 13-week check
lines: List each of the next thirteen weeks.
Start with today's cash, add what you expect to receive, and subtract what you must pay.
Each week's closing balance becomes the next week's opening balance.

scenes.heading: Read it every Monday

items: Enter receipts on the date you expect the money
Mark the first week that goes below your safety level
Act before that week: chase, delay or arrange funding

lines: Enter receipts on the date you expect the money, not the invoice date.
Find the first week that falls below your safety level.
That week tells you how much time you have to act.
